public_rationale: The claim is that scaling, RAG, and prompting had not eliminated hallucinations by late 2024. Vendors had marketed RAG legal tools as 'eliminating' hallucinations or as 'hallucination-free'. A preregistered Stanford study found those tools still hallucinated 17–33% of the time. OpenAI's own system card says its newest scaled models hallucinate 'less frequently' than GPT-4o, not never; its table gives o1-preview a 0.44 rate on SimpleQA. I found no evidence of any system with near-zero hallucination on broad tests by the post date.
limitations: 'Eliminated' is a high bar that makes the claim easy to support. Real reductions did happen.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: None of the industry's efforts (scaling, RAG, prompting) has eliminated hallucinations.

statement.excerpt: None of this has eliminated the problem.

our_interpretation: 'This' refers to the mitigations named just before: scaling, more scaling, RAG, and system-prompt instructions such as Apple's 'do not hallucinate'.
Plain reading: as of the post date, no system using these methods had brought hallucinations down to zero or near zero.
Target period: the GPT-4o era up to the post date (2024-05-13 to 2024-11-28).
criteria.support_condition: 2024 evaluations showing that scaled models and RAG systems still had clearly non-zero hallucination rates.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A scaled, RAG-based, or prompt-mitigated system shown by late 2024 to have a near-zero hallucination rate on broad, standard evaluations.
